title: 2023 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: Circle \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) each have radius \(1,\) and the distance between their centers is \(\tfrac12.\) Circle \(C_3\) is the largest circle internally tangent to both \(C_1\) and \(C_2.\) Circle \(C_4\) is internally tangent to both \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) and externally tangent to \(C_3.\) What is the radius of \(C_4?\)

solutions.text:
Put the centers at \(O_1=\left(-\tfrac14,0\right)\) and \(O_2=\left(\tfrac14,0\right).\) By symmetry \(C_3\) is centered at the origin, and internal tangency to \(C_1\) gives radius \(1-\tfrac14=\tfrac34.\)

Let \(C_4\) have radius \(r,\) centered at \((0,k)\) on the axis of symmetry. External tangency to \(C_3\) gives \(k=\tfrac34+r,\) and internal tangency to \(C_1\) gives \(\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{16}+k^2}=1-r.\)

Substituting, \(\tfrac{1}{16}+\left(\tfrac34+r\right)^2=(1-r)^2,\) which simplifies to \(\tfrac72 r=\tfrac38,\) so \(r=\dfrac{3}{28}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: By symmetry \(C_3\) is centered at the midpoint of \(C_1C_2;\) its radius is \(1-\tfrac14=\tfrac34\)
Place \(C_4\) on the perpendicular bisector; its center is \(1-r\) from a unit circle’s center and \(\tfrac34+r\) from the center of \(C_3\)
